record.paper_title: The Erdős-Ulam problem, Lang's conjecture, and uniformity
record.context_brief: Seven-point rational distance set in general position
record.original_question: Does there exist a set S of seven points in R^2 such that every pairwise Euclidean distance between points of S is rational, no three points of S lie on one line, and no four points of S lie on one circle?

evidence.quote: A rational distance set is a subset S of R2 such that the distance between any two points of S is a rational number.
For example, a set of seven points in R2 is in general position if and only if no 7 − 4 = 3 points lie on a line and no 7 − 3 = 4 points lie on a circle.
Erdős famously asked whether there exists a rational distance set with seven elements in general position.
Erdős’ question was answered in the aﬃrmative by Kreisel and Kurz [ KK08].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A rational distance set is a finite subset $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a rational number. A set of seven points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is said to be in general position if no three of them are collinear and no four of them lie on a common circle.

Question: Does there exist a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of seven points that is simultaneously a rational distance set and in general position?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed by Erdős and answered affirmatively by Kreisel and Kurz (2008), who explicitly constructed a seven-point rational distance set in general position (no 3 on a line, no 4 on a circle). The analogous question for 8 or more points remains open.

status_evidence.title: Kreisel & Kurz, 'There are integral heptagons, no three points on a line, no four on a circle'
status_evidence.snippet: We present a set of seven points in the plane such that all pairwise distances are integers, no three points are collinear, and no four points are concyclic.
status_evidence.claim: Kreisel and Kurz constructed an explicit such 7-point configuration, solving Erdős's question.

status_evidence.title: The Erdős-Ulam problem, Lang's conjecture and uniformity (arXiv:1901.02616)
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős' question was answered in the affirmative by Kreisel and Kurz.
status_evidence.claim: The seven-point case is acknowledged as solved.
